evidence_chain: Eaton’s Q1 2026 press release reported record Electrical Americas sales of $3.6 billion, up 20% year over year; organic sales growth was 14%, acquisitions added 5%, and foreign exchange added 1%. Source: https://www.eaton.com/us/en-us/company/news-insights/news-releases/2026/eaton-reports-record-first-quarter-2026-results.html

The same Q1 2026 release reported Electrical Americas operating profit of $922 million and operating margin of 25.6%, useful for tracking whether backlog conversion translates into profitability. Source: https://www.eaton.com/us/en-us/company/news-insights/news-releases/2026/eaton-reports-record-first-quarter-2026-results.html

Eaton disclosed that Electrical Americas 12-month rolling average orders were up 42% organically in Q1 2026 and total backlog at the end of March 2026 was up 44% over March 2025. Source: https://www.eaton.com/us/en-us/company/news-insights/news-releases/2026/eaton-reports-record-first-quarter-2026-results.html

Eaton disclosed that the rolling 12-month book-to-bill ratio for the Electrical businesses increased to 1.2 in Q1 2026, indicating orders continued to exceed billings on a rolling basis. Source: https://www.eaton.com/us/en-us/company/news-insights/news-releases/2026/eaton-reports-record-first-quarter-2026-results.html

Eaton’s Q1 2026 analyst presentation states that Electrical Americas data-center orders were up approximately 240% and data-center revenue was also up materially, supporting the cached evidence that data-center demand is entering orders/backlog rather than remaining only a narrative. Source: https://www.eaton.com/content/dam/eaton/company/investor-relations/quarterly-earnings/filings/2026/q1/q1-2026-analyst-presentation.pdf

Eaton’s 2025 Form 10-K/annual-report disclosure describes Electrical Americas as including electrical components, industrial components, power distribution and assemblies, residential products, single-phase power quality and connectivity, three-phase power quality, wiring devices, circuit protection, utility power distribution, power reliability equipment, and services produced and sold primarily in North and South America. Source: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1551182/000155118226000007/etn-20251231.htm

Eaton’s 2025 annual-report disclosure identifies data centers and distributed IT among the principal markets for Electrical Americas and Electrical Global, along with commercial and institutional, industrial, utilities, residential, and machinery OEM markets. Source: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1551182/000155118226000007/etn-20251231.htm

Because data-center energization depends on electrical equipment availability, the combination of strong Electrical Americas orders, backlog expansion, book-to-bill above 1.0, and specific data-center order acceleration supports Eaton as a chokepoint candidate rather than a purely downstream AI beneficiary.

【待验证current disclosures do not fully isolate product-level revenue/backlog from switchgear, UPS, busway, power distribution, and data-center electrical systems; this remains the main evidence gap before assigning a higher-purity chokepoint score.
falsification_plan: Downgrade the thesis if Electrical Americas order growth decelerates sharply for multiple quarters while management commentary on data-center demand weakens.
Downgrade the thesis if Electrical business book-to-bill falls to or below 1.0 for multiple quarters and backlog growth normalizes without offsetting revenue/margin acceleration.
Downgrade the thesis if backlog converts into revenue but Electrical Americas margin does not expand or deteriorates due to price-cost lag, mix, manufacturing inefficiency, or competitive pressure.

Downgrade the thesis if management disclosures show that the apparent data-center upside is mostly broad electrical-cycle strength rather than switchgear, distribution, UPS, busway, and data-center power-system content.

Downgrade the thesis if lead times for switchgear, power distribution, UPS, transformers, or related equipment shorten materially because supply catches up, but Eaton does not show corresponding revenue or profit realization.
Downgrade the thesis if competitors report faster capacity additions, share gains, or pricing pressure in the same data-center electrical categories.
Downgrade the thesis if large hyperscaler, colocation, utility, EPC, or distributor orders are cancelled, pushed out, or replaced by lower-margin framework agreements.
Downgrade the thesis if acquisition integration, especially around data-center thermal/power adjacencies, distracts from core electrical execution or dilutes segment margins.
next_research_tasks: Pull Eaton’s latest 10-Q and earnings-call transcript after Q1 2026 to extract exact Electrical Americas backlog, orders, book-to-bill, pricing, lead-time, and margin commentary.

Build a product-level exposure table for switchgear, power distribution assemblies, UPS/power quality, busway, utility power distribution, power reliability equipment, data-center thermal/power systems, and services.
Estimate data-center revenue and backlog purity by triangulating management commentary, investor presentations, customer examples, product pages, and channel/EPC disclosures.

Compare Eaton’s electrical backlog growth, order growth, and margin trajectory with Schneider Electric, Siemens, ABB, Vertiv, Hubbell, Powell Industries, nVent, and Wesco to determine whether Eaton has relative chokepoint control or simply participates in a broad industry upcycle.

Track lead-time evidence from distributors, electrical contractors, EPC commentary, project filings, and customer procurement discussions for medium-voltage switchgear, transformers, UPS, busway, and power-distribution systems.
Review Eaton’s capacity-expansion disclosures, capex, new facilities, hiring, and supply-chain investments to judge whether supply remains constrained or the bottleneck is being relieved.
Map large data-center project pipelines by geography against Eaton’s manufacturing and service footprint, focusing on U.S. Electrical Americas exposure.
Monitor future quarterly disclosures for data-center order growth, data-center revenue growth, backlog conversion, cancellation/deferral language, and Electrical Americas margin bridge.
Check whether recent acquisitions such as Boyd Thermal and Resilient Power Systems increase Eaton’s data-center system-level content or introduce integration and margin dilution risk.
Create a falsification dashboard with thresholds for Electrical Americas order growth, backlog growth, book-to-bill, segment margin, data-center mix, and lead-time commentary.

deep_reports.supply_chain_position: Theme node: New Hotspots → AI/data-center power infrastructure → grid-to-building electrical chain → medium/low-voltage switchgear, power distribution assemblies, utility power distribution, UPS/power quality, busway, power reliability equipment, data-center electrical systems and services. Downstream customers and channels likely include hyperscalers, colocation operators, utilities, EPCs, electrical contractors, distributors, and large industrial/commercial customers. Upstream constraints to monitor include transformer and switchgear component availability, manufacturing capacity, copper and electrical components, testing/certification throughput, field-service capacity, and long customer qualification cycles. Public-market mapping: ETN is an integrated electrical-equipment manufacturer with broad exposure across Electrical Americas and Electrical Global; comparable or adjacent research references include Schneider Electric, Siemens, ABB, Vertiv, Hubbell, nVent, Powell Industries, Wesco, and electrical contractors/EPCs, but this report does not rank or recommend securities.
deep_reports.thesis_cn: Eaton 是 AI 与数据中心扩张中“电网接入—开关柜—配电—UPS/电力管理—机柜供电”链条的高纯度公开市场研究标的之一。其价值不在于泛泛受益于数据中心建设，而在于部分产品处在项目通电、交付和扩容的关键路径上：开关柜、配电系统、三相电能质量设备、UPS、母线槽、功率可靠性设备和相关服务。已验证的公司披露显示，2026 年 Q1 Electrical Americas 销售额同比增长 20%，该分部 12 个月滚动平均订单有机增长 42%，积压订单同比增长 44%，Electrical 业务 12 个月滚动 book-to-bill 达 1.2；公司 Q1 2026 投资者材料还披露 Electrical Americas 数据中心订单约增长 240%。因此，Eaton 的核心研究问题应从“是否受益于 AI 数据中心”升级为“其增长与利润释放中，有多少来自真正供给紧张、验证周期长、交付能力稀缺的电气设备环节”。
deep_reports.thesis_en: [Inference] Eaton is a relatively high-purity public-market research target for the AI/data-center grid-to-rack electrical bottleneck: grid interconnection support, switchgear, power distribution, UPS/power quality, busway, power-reliability equipment, and related services. The thesis is not simply that Eaton benefits from data-center capex; it is that some of its products sit on the critical path for energizing and scaling data centers. Verified company disclosures show Q1 2026 Electrical Americas sales up 20% year over year, 12-month rolling average organic orders up 42%, backlog up 44%, and a 1.2 book-to-bill ratio for Electrical businesses. Eaton’s Q1 2026 investor presentation also disclosed approximately 240% growth in Electrical Americas data-center orders. The key research task is to separate true scarcity-linked switchgear/power-chain exposure from a broader electrical-cycle uplift.
deep_reports.title_cn: Eaton：AI 数据中心从电网到机柜供电链条的电气基础设施卡点
deep_reports.title_en: Eaton: Grid-to-Rack Electrical Infrastructure Chokepoint for AI Data Centers

evidence_chain: Fact: GE Vernova reported Q1 2026 orders of $18.3B, up 71% organically, and backlog growth of $13.0B sequentially, including $5B from Prolec GE. Source: GE Vernova Q1 2026 press release, https://www.gevernova.com/sites/default/files/gev_webcast_pressrelease_04222026.pdf

Fact: Management stated that Q1 2026 Electrification booked $2.4B in equipment orders to support data centers, more than all of last year. Source: GE Vernova Q1 2026 press release, https://www.gevernova.com/sites/default/files/gev_webcast_pressrelease_04222026.pdf

Fact: GE Vernova Q1 2026 presentation shows Electrification backlog rising from $34B in 2025 to $42B in Q1 2026 and identifies HVDC systems, substations, switchgear, transformers, capacitors, grid monitoring, digitization, synchronous condensers, and battery storage as relevant offerings. Source: GE Vernova Q1 2026 presentation, https://www.gevernova.com/sites/default/files/gev_webcast_presentation_04222026.pdf

Fact: The Q1 2026 presentation states Gas Power backlog increased to 44GW and slot reservations increased to 56GW. Source: GE Vernova Q1 2026 presentation, https://www.gevernova.com/sites/default/files/gev_webcast_presentation_04222026.pdf

Fact: SEC filing text states GE Vernova completed the acquisition of the remaining 50% stake in Prolec GE on February 2, 2026 for cash consideration of $5.254B; Prolec GE produces transformers and transformer components for generation, transmission, and distribution of electricity and is now included in Electrification. Source: SEC filing excerpt, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1996810/000199681026000064/R16.htm

Fact: Industry coverage of the same Q1 2026 disclosure says Electrification produces substations, switchgear, transformers and HVDC systems, with $2.4B of Q1 data-center-related orders and $7.1B total Electrification orders. Source: Power Engineering, https://www.power-eng.com/gas/turbines/data-centers-drive-record-surge-in-ge-vernova-power-equipment-orders-as-turbine-slots-tighten-through-2030/

Inference: The evidence is strongest for order momentum and product mapping; it is weaker for precise end-market attribution because public materials still mix data-center demand with broader utility, IPP, industrial, and grid-modernization demand.
Hypothesis: GE Vernova's strongest chokepoint value may come from combined exposure to both grid equipment and gas-power slot scarcity rather than from any single product category.
falsification_plan: Downgrade thesis if future filings or calls show Q1 2026 data-center Electrification orders were unusually large, non-recurring, or not repeated across subsequent quarters.

Downgrade thesis if management cannot provide clearer segmentation of data-center orders/backlog versus utility grid modernization, industrial electrification, renewables integration, and general replacement demand.

Downgrade thesis if Electrification backlog grows but segment EBITDA margin fails to improve or declines because of low-margin mix, Prolec GE integration costs, tariffs, execution issues, or inflation.
Downgrade thesis if transformer and switchgear lead times normalize materially faster than data-center load growth and interconnection demand.
Downgrade thesis if Gas Power slot reservation agreements do not convert into firm orders, or if data-center-linked gas projects are delayed/canceled at a high rate.
Downgrade thesis if HVDC/substation project awards slip due to permitting, utility approvals, EPC bottlenecks, or regulatory pushback.
Downgrade thesis if cash conversion weakens materially despite rising backlog, implying working-capital or execution strain.

Downgrade thesis if alternative architectures such as behind-the-meter fuel cells, modular nuclear, geothermal, batteries, or non-GEV turbine suppliers capture a larger share of incremental data-center power demand than expected.
next_research_tasks: Pull GE Vernova Q1 2026 10-Q and extract segment RPO/backlog, order growth, Prolec GE contribution, working-capital drivers, and risk-factor changes.
Track Q2 and Q3 2026 disclosures for repeatability of data-center-specific Electrification orders after the $2.4B Q1 figure.
Create a backlog attribution table: data centers, utilities, IPPs, industrial electrification, renewables/grid modernization, and other end markets.
Map Prolec GE facilities, announced transformer expansions, expected capacity timing, and product categories: distribution, medium power, large power, and components.
Track transformer and switchgear lead-time indicators from utilities, EPCs, and competitors to test whether scarcity persists.
Track Gas Power slot reservations: total GW, firm backlog GW, reservation GW, data-center share, conversion rate, pricing commentary, and 2029/2030 capacity availability.
Identify named HVDC, substation, and grid-modernization project awards involving GE Vernova and tag which are data-center-linked versus general grid investment.
Monitor Electrification revenue, EBITDA margin, equipment backlog, book-to-bill, Prolec GE integration costs, and mix commentary each quarter.
Monitor Wind losses, tariff impact, and contract-loss commentary to determine whether non-core drag offsets Power/Electrification upside.

Compare GEV exposure against other public-market nodes in the same AI-power chain, such as transformer suppliers, electrical contractors, switchgear providers, gas-turbine peers, and utility-scale power developers, without making buy/sell recommendations.
risks: Attribution risk: data-center-related orders may be a smaller or less recurring share of backlog than the headline suggests once broader utility and industrial demand are separated.
Backlog-conversion risk: orders and slot reservations may not convert into revenue, free cash flow, or margin at the expected cadence.
Capacity-normalization risk: transformer, switchgear, substation, HVDC, or turbine supply additions could reduce lead times faster than expected.
Execution risk: large grid and power projects have long engineering, procurement, construction, permitting, and interconnection timelines; delays could shift revenue or compress margins.
Mix risk: Prolec GE integration, lower-margin grid projects, cost inflation, or project losses could dilute the profitability of Electrification backlog.
Gas-power conversion risk: slot reservations may fail to become binding orders, especially if data-center projects are delayed, canceled, or switch to alternative power architectures.
Regulatory and community risk: data-center power projects face interconnection constraints, local opposition, environmental permitting, and utility rate-base scrutiny.
Segment drag risk: Wind remains a potential EBITDA and execution drag; GE Vernova's Q1 2026 materials note Wind EBITDA losses and tariff impact.
Market-pricing risk: the equity may already price a large portion of AI-power upside, so research priority should focus on evidence upgrades/downgrades rather than price targets.
deep_reports.supply_chain_position: Demand layer: hyperscale and colocation data centers requiring large, reliable power connections. Infrastructure layer: utilities, IPPs, industrial power customers, EPCs, and grid operators. GE Vernova nodes: 1) Electrification / Grid Systems Integration: HVDC systems, substations, grid integration; 2) Power Transmission: switchgear, transformers, capacitors, including Prolec GE transformer capacity; 3) Grid Automation & Software: monitoring, digitization, predictive and autonomous grid management; 4) Power Conversion & Storage: synchronous condensers, battery storage and resiliency equipment; 5) Power: gas turbines, upgrades, services, and slot reservations for future dispatchable generation. Chokepoint hypothesis: data centers pull simultaneously on grid connection equipment and generation capacity, making GE Vernova a broad beneficiary if orders convert into profitable backlog.
deep_reports.thesis_cn: 推论：GE Vernova 可能是 AI 数据中心新增负荷外溢到电力系统后的多节点卡点公司。其 Electrification 覆盖 HVDC、变电站、开关柜、变压器、电网自动化与储能/电能转换，Power 覆盖燃气轮机和服务。官方 Q1 2026 信息显示 Electrification 单季有 24 亿美元数据中心相关设备订单，且 Electrification backlog 从 2025 年末 340 亿美元升至 2026Q1 的 420 亿美元；同时 Gas Power backlog 与 slot reservation agreements 合计从 83GW 增至 100GW。若 AI 数据中心建设继续受电力接入、变压器、并网和可调度电源限制约束，GE Vernova 的优势在于它不是单一设备暴露，而是横跨多个必须采购、验证周期长、项目周期长的节点。研究难点是分辨 AI 数据中心需求、传统公用事业电网升级、工业电气化和周期性补库之间的真实贡献。
deep_reports.thesis_en: Inference: GE Vernova may be a multi-node chokepoint company as AI data-center load growth spills into the power system. Its Electrification segment spans HVDC, substations, switchgear, transformers, grid automation, and power conversion/storage, while Power adds gas turbines and services. Official Q1 2026 materials show $2.4 billion of Electrification equipment orders tied to data centers, Electrification backlog rising from $34 billion at year-end 2025 to $42 billion in Q1 2026, and Gas Power backlog plus slot reservation agreements increasing from 83GW to 100GW. If AI data-center deployment remains constrained by grid interconnection, transformers, substations, and dispatchable generation, GE Vernova has broader bottleneck exposure than a single-equipment supplier. The hard part is attribution: separating data-center-driven demand from traditional utility grid modernization, industrial electrification, and cyclical equipment demand.
deep_reports.title_cn: GE Vernova：AI 电力扩张中的多节点卡点候选
deep_reports.title_en: GE Vernova: Multi-Node Chokepoint Candidate in the AI Power Buildout

evidence_chain: [Fact | official source] PUCO announced on 2025-07-09 that it ordered AEP Ohio to file new tariffs applying to data centers, adopted a settlement involving AEP Ohio, PUCO staff, OCC and others, and recognized unprecedented load growth requiring significant electric transmission infrastructure. Source: https://content.govdelivery.com/accounts/OHPUC/bulletins/3e8bb79

[Fact | official source] PUCO stated the tariff order was intended to safeguard non-data-center customers from cost-shifting risks tied to underused investments made for data-center load. Source: https://content.govdelivery.com/accounts/OHPUC/bulletins/3e8bb79

[Fact | official company source] AEP Ohio’s Data Center Tariff webpage describes the process: customers request a load study, pay a $10,000 to $100,000 study fee depending on requested capacity, receive a service plan, then have 60 days to sign a Letter of Agreement and Electric Service Agreement. Source: https://www.aepohio.com/company/about/rates/data-center-tariff/

[Fact | official company source] AEP Ohio states that the Letter of Agreement requires customers to reimburse 100% of buildout costs if they cancel or delay the project by more than 12 months before the target energization date. Source: https://www.aepohio.com/company/about/rates/data-center-tariff/

[Fact | official company source] AEP Ohio’s tariff page states the initial contract term equals the load ramp period, no greater than four years, plus eight years; the ramp period contract capacity floor rises from 50% in year one to 90% in year four. Source: https://www.aepohio.com/company/about/rates/data-center-tariff/

[Fact | official company source] AEP Ohio states that customers lacking specified credit strength and cash thresholds must provide a guarantee or collateral equal to 50% of total minimum charges for the full contract term. Source: https://www.aepohio.com/company/about/rates/data-center-tariff/

[Fact | official company source] AEP Ohio states monthly billing demand is subject to minimum demand-charge mechanics and cannot exceed 85% of total contract capacity. Source: https://www.aepohio.com/company/about/rates/data-center-tariff/

[Fact | official company source] AEP Ohio’s February 13, 2026 update says that, as of February 12, 2026, data centers or developers had signed binding contracts for 5,642 MW under the Data Center Tariff. Source: https://www.aepohio.com/company/news/view?releaseID=10753

[Fact | official company source] The same AEP Ohio update says 5,642 MW is in addition to 12,219 MW of data-center contracts signed before the tariff went into effect, for 17,861 MW total contracted data-center projects scheduled progressively through 2035. Source: https://www.aepohio.com/company/news/view?releaseID=10753

[Fact | official company source] AEP Ohio says early data-center requests exceeded 30,000 MW; after the first tariff step, 13,022.7 MW requested and paid for formal engineering studies; after legal and financial commitments, that fell to 5,642 MW. Source: https://www.aepohio.com/company/news/view?releaseID=10753

[Fact | official company source] AEP’s investor page, crawled in June 2026, states a five-year capital plan of $78 billion and 63 GW of new load by 2030 backed by signed agreements. Source: https://www.aep.com/investors/

[Inference] Evidence quality is relatively high for the existence of the tariff, contract process, and signed-MW figures because the strongest sources are PUCO and AEP Ohio. Evidence quality is lower for ultimate earnings impact because signed MW still must convert into energized load, approved investment, allowed returns, and timely cost recovery.
falsification_plan: 如果未来几个季度 AEP Ohio 的 signed binding MW 停滞、下降，或大量项目从合同队列中退出，则下调 thesis 强度。
如果 5,642 MW DCT 合同和 12,219 MW pre-tariff 合同未能按披露节奏转化为 energized MW，则判断从“可兑现瓶颈”降级为“排队故事”。
如果 PUCO/FERC/PJM 或州监管裁决限制数据中心相关 capex 的成本回收、allowed return 或 rate-base inclusion，则下调经济价值判断。
如果 minimum bill、exit fee、LOA reimbursement、collateral 或 ESA 条款在实际取消/延期案例中未能保护 AEP 和其他客户，则下调证据质量。
如果电网设备供应链、许可、选址、输电线路反对或施工瓶颈导致关键项目大幅延后，则下调 2026-2030 capex 转化可见度。
如果 AEP 的增长主要来自更高融资需求、权益发行或利息成本，而不是可回收 rate base 和实际负荷增长，则下调股东经济弹性。
如果数据中心客户更多采用自备电源、燃料电池、独立发电、储能或迁移到其他州/市场，导致 AEP 服务区内用电承诺减少，则下调需求侧 thesis。
如果居民或工业用户反弹推动立法或监管机构要求数据中心承担更多 upfront contribution，且该机制减少 AEP 可投资 rate-base，则重新评估商业模式映射。
next_research_tasks: Track quarterly changes in AEP Ohio signed binding MW, pre-tariff MW, new study requests, study-fee-paid MW, signed ESA/LOA MW, and energized MW.
Build a timeline from 2026-02-12 contracted MW to expected energization dates through 2035; separate load already energized from load only contractually scheduled.
Pull PUCO docket 24-508-EL-ATA and extract final order details: minimum demand, collateral, exit fee, cost allocation, rehearing/appeal status, and intervenor objections.
Compare AEP Ohio Schedule DCT with large-load tariff proposals or rules in Virginia, Texas/ERCOT, Duke Energy Ohio, Dominion, and other PJM/SPP/ERCOT utilities.
Map which AEP jurisdictions besides Ohio have large-load tariffs, signed agreements, or data-center-driven capex plans; separate Ohio-specific evidence from consolidated AEP evidence.
Reconcile AEP’s $78 billion 2026-2030 capital plan and 63 GW new-load disclosure with rate-base growth, allowed ROE, equity issuance needs, and debt metrics.
Identify which portions of AEP capex are transmission, distribution, generation, customer-specific facilities, and PJM/RTO-approved projects; tag each by regulatory approval status.
Monitor PUCO/FERC/PJM filings for transmission upgrade approvals, cost allocation disputes, interconnection milestones, and service-date delays.
Check whether customers must provide parent guarantees, letters of credit, cash collateral, or sponsor co-signatures; assess enforceability by customer type.

Create a dashboard series: requested MW → study-fee-paid MW → signed LOA/ESA MW → collateral posted → approved capex → construction start → energized MW → actual load factor → revenue/rate-base contribution.
Stress-test whether rising power bills or capacity charges create political backlash that could change tariff design or cost recovery.
Review AEP earnings calls and 10-K/10-Q risk factors for language changes around large-load contractual commitments, construction risk, regulatory lag, financing costs, and customer creditworthiness.
risks: 客户执行风险：signed binding contracts 仍可能出现延期、缩容、转让、退出或争议；合同强度高于普通意向书，但不等于已送电负荷。
监管风险：PUCO、FERC、PJM 或其他州监管机构可能限制、延迟或重新分配数据中心相关输配电投资的成本回收。
成本转嫁政治风险：若居民、商业或工业客户认为数据中心推高电费，可能带来听证、立法、费率设计调整或更严格的大负荷 tariff。
建设周期风险：输电、变电站、配电升级、变压器和开关设备供应链可能延误，导致 energization date 后移。
资本开支质量风险：capex 增长不自动等于股东经济价值；关键在 allowed ROE、rate-base inclusion、AFUDC、滞后回收、融资成本和稀释压力。
负荷预测风险：AI 算力需求、芯片效率、数据中心利用率、液冷/电源架构、behind-the-meter generation 或地理迁移可能改变实际用电曲线。
信用与抵押风险：collateral 与 minimum bill 机制若遇到客户破产、项目公司结构复杂、担保主体不足或法律挑战，保护力度可能弱于表面条款。
市场定价风险：AEP 已公开披露大量新负荷和资本计划，市场可能已部分定价；本报告只给研究优先级，不提供买卖建议或目标价格。
deep_reports.supply_chain_position: Theme: New Hotspots / AI infrastructure power. Demand driver: hyperscale and AI data-center electricity demand. System layer: regional power grid and utility service territory. Chokepoint node: grid interconnection, load-study queue discipline, transmission and distribution upgrade planning, customer-backed minimum billing, collateral, and cost recovery. Public-market mapping: AEP is a regulated utility with AEP Ohio as a high-signal operating subsidiary for data-center load conversion; upstream beneficiaries may include transmission equipment, transformers, switchgear, EPC, grid engineering, generation, storage, and fuel supply, but this report focuses on AEP as the regulated grid-access and cost-recovery node.
deep_reports.thesis_cn: AEP 的 Serenity 卡点 thesis 不是简单押注电价或数据中心建设，而是押注大型新增负荷正在把电网接入、输电扩容、配电升级、客户信用支持和监管成本分摊变成可跟踪的产业瓶颈。缓存证据显示，截至 2026-02-12，AEP Ohio 将早期超过 30,000 MW 的数据中心用电意向，筛选为 5,642 MW 的 Schedule DCT 下已签 binding contracts；AEP Ohio 还披露另有 12,219 MW 是 tariff 生效前已签的数据中心合同，因此合计 contracted data-center projects 为 17,861 MW，并计划逐步在 2035 年前上线。官方页面显示 Schedule DCT 通过 load study fee、LOA、ESA、collateral、minimum demand charge、exit fee 等机制，把过去较松散的负荷意向转化为更强的法律和财务承诺。真正要验证的是：这些合同 MW 是否变成送电负荷、AEP 是否获得输配电和相关投资的监管批准、以及成本回收是否被 PUCO/FERC/PJM 等监管和市场机制接受。
deep_reports.thesis_en: [Inference] AEP is a clean chokepoint mapping for the AI/data-center power theme because the key scarce resource is not only electricity generation, but grid access: interconnection studies, transmission upgrades, distribution buildout, customer credit support, and regulated cost recovery. Cached evidence and AEP Ohio’s February 13, 2026 update state that, as of February 12, 2026, data centers or developers signed binding contracts for 5,642 MW under AEP Ohio’s Data Center Tariff, down from more than 30,000 MW of earlier expressed interest; AEP Ohio also reported 12,219 MW of pre-tariff data-center contracts, for 17,861 MW total contracted data-center projects scheduled to come online progressively through 2035. The thesis is strongest if signed MW converts into energized MW and approved rate-base growth. It weakens if customers defer, contracts prove less enforceable than expected, regulators restrict recovery, or required grid upgrades slip materially.
